model.title: Widths 1.2, 1.8, 2.1, 1.9, 3.0 m. Find the mean, median and range.

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: Mean 2.0 m, median 1.9 m, range 1.8 m

questions.q: Describe the trend in the practice width data.
questions.a: Width generally increases downstream from 1.2 m to 3.0 m (1), with an anomaly at site 4 (1.9 m) (1)
questions.model: Overall direction: increases downstream. Use data: 1.2 m at site 1 to 3.0 m at site 5. Note the anomaly: site 4 dips to 1.9 m.

questions.q: Suggest one reason for the anomaly at site 4.
questions.a: For example: hard rock narrowing the channel (1), or a measuring error at that site (1)

questions.q: Does the data support 'channel width increases downstream'?
questions.a: Mostly yes: the overall trend increases despite one anomaly

questions.q: Core: Section B practice on unfamiliar data on the portal: complete a graph, calculate statistics, describe the pattern, evaluate the conclusion.
questions.a: Indicative mark points in the portal key
questions.model: Teacher does the first part: plot the missing point accurately and add the axis label with units.

questions.q: Extend: 'Evaluate the reliability of your conclusions.' Plan in bullet points.
questions.a: Strengths: repeated measures, systematic sampling; weaknesses: few sites, one day, equipment error; overall judgement on reliability

questions.q: Stretch: How could GIS or secondary data strengthen the conclusion?
questions.a: Compare with long-term gauge data or maps (1) to check the pattern is not just one day's result (1)

questions.q: Big question: how do you turn numbers into a conclusion you can defend?
questions.a: Present data clearly, use statistics to describe patterns and anomalies, answer the question with evidence and judge how reliable it is
